text:
Mira: Heads-up — nightly perf job flagged a cache pressure spike during continuous batching prefetch. saw OOM guard trips + kernel fallback at 03:12 UTC. profile link: https://perf.example/redwood/123 :eyes:
ops-bot: [ALERT] node-gpu-34: kv_cache_used jumped 1.8x in 60s; soft-oom events=3; fallback_kernels=2
Jonas: ugh. is this the prefetch heuristic that warms KV for long-context requests?
Mira: yes. reproducer: mix of many long chats + a few short completions. prefetcher was aggressively touching prefixes for predicted next-turn tokens, pushed net KV footprin g up. summary from perf job:
```
alloc_snapshot: kv_prefetch_bytes +1.2GiB in 45s
batch_formation: avg_wait_ms 8 -> 6 (good)
oom_guard: fired when free_kv_bytes < 600MiB
kernel_route: moved 12% of batches to fallback quant path
```
Jonas: key constraint seems to be memory headroom not tokens. We trade latency for memory now.
Sam: thoughts — can we gate prefetch by `kv_free_bytes` threshold and shrink per-request prefetch window? like prefer in-batch locality over aggressive cross-batch prefetch.
Priya: agree. maybe adapt prefetch size proportional to `kv_free_bytes / kv_capacity`. e.g. `prefetch_tokens = base_prefetch * max(0.2, kv_free_frac)`
Mira: also caused weird kernel-select churn; when fallback kernel used, end-to-end latency spiked for those batches. So two failure modes: OOM attempts and kernel-route oscillation.
Jonas: proposal: admission controller checks (a) kv_free_bytes > headroom_target, (b) estimated_prefetch_delta + current_inflight_prefetch < soft_limit. If not satisfied, mark request as "low-prefetch" and reduce prefetch to 0 or 8 tokens.
Sam: we already have a `batch_token_budget` per queue. Could we add a secondary `kv_token_budget` that counts estimated KV entries touched by prefetch? then admission uses min(batch_budget, kv_budget)
Priya: small requests (<=128 tokens) should be prioritized under pressure since they have smaller KV footprints. New queue policy: when kv_free_frac < 0.25, prefer short-first and reduce batch_window_ms to avoid compounding prefetch.
Mira: sketch of config for a soft canary:
```
prefetch: {
  enabled: dynamic,
  base_prefetch: 32,
  min_prefetch: 0,
  headroom_target_bytes: 800MiB,
  canary_fraction: 0.10
}
admission: {
  kv_budget_bytes: 512MiB,
  short_request_threshold: 128,
  fallback_prefetch_tokens: 8
}
```
Jonas: metrics to add: `kv_prefetch_delta`, `kv_inflight_prefetch`, `admit_reasons.kv_headroom`, `kernel_route_churn` — we need these to correlate regressions.
Sam: testing plan: 1) unit-tests for admission logic, 2) offline sim with realistic trace (use 24h-prod-sample), 3) 10% canary on a dedicated pool for 4h with `headroom_target_bytes` bumped to 1GiB to be conservative.
Priya: one safety tweak — if fallback kernel rate > 5% in canary, rollback immediately and mark as P0.
Mira: will open PR with admission controller + metric emits + config flags. also will add a quick CLI probe to query `kv_free_bytes` and `kv_inflight_prefetch` per node: `ri node probe --node node-gpu-34 --metrics kv_free_bytes,kv_inflight_prefetch`.
Jonas: nice. for telemetry, push the perf job snapshots to a dashboard panel `batching:kv_pressure` and annotate events when we flip queue policy.
Sam: minor: consider transient backoff for prefetch on repeated soft-ooms per node — exponential backoff for prefetch duration.
Priya: +1. also add guard in kernel selector: if a batch contains mix of low-prefetch and full-prefetch requests, avoid instantaneous kernel-route change; wait for next batch to switch (hysteresis).
Mira: Action items:
- Mira: open PR with admission + flags + canary config (today)
- Sam: add metrics and offline sim harness (tomorrow)
- Jonas: dashboard panels + alert rule for kernel_route_churn (48h)
- Priya: add canary rollback check + hysteresis in kernel selector (EOW)
ops-bot: scheduled canary rollout 10% for cluster 'dedicated-prefetch-canary' starting 1719138000 UTC
Mira: cool, I'll drop notes in the PR and link the perf traces. thanks all :+1:
Jonas: thanks — let's monitor closely and post back numbers after the canary runs.
